We need to parse the problem: There is a tournament with teams 0 to n-1. Given a boolean matrix grid of size n*n. For i != j, grid[i][j] == 1 means team i is defeated by team j (i.e., team j defeats team i). Or wait: The problem states: "For all i, j that 0 <= i, j <= n - 1 and i!= j team i will be defeated by team j if grid[i][j] == 1, otherwise, team i will defeat team j." So if grid[i][j]==1, team i loses to team j, i.e., j defeats i. If grid[i][j]==0, team i defeats team j (since not 1). So we can interpret grid[i][j]==1 as edge from j -> i (j beats i). Conversely, grid[i][j]==0 as edge i -> j (i beats j). The matrix is anti-symmetric: grid[i][j] != grid[j][i] for i!=j (so exactly one direction is 1, the other 0). Also transitivity holds: if a beats b and b beats c then a beats c.

Thus the relation defines a total order (strict weak ordering) among teams: a strict total order (since for any pair, one beats the other). Because anti-symmetric and transitive yields a strict total order (a linear order). So there is a unique "champion": the team that defeats all others (i.e., no one beats it). The problem asks: "Team a will be defeated in the tournament if there is no team b that is weaker than team a. Return the team that will be defeated in the tournament."
